questions.def: With 'the more... the...', use comparative adjective/adverb forms.
questions.question: The more you practice, the ___ you become.

questions.def: 'Far' modifies comparatives like 'more reliable' for emphasis.
questions.question: This car is ___ than the one I had before.

questions.def: Use the superlative form ('best') with 'ever' to express maximum degree.
questions.question: This is the ___ book I have ever read.

questions.def: Use 'as...as' in affirmative and negative comparisons of equality.
questions.question: She is not ___ intelligent as her brother.

questions.def: Use 'the more... the more...' for parallel increases.
questions.question: The ___ I study, the more I realize I don't know.

questions.def: Use '-er' for short adjectives in comparative forms (easier).
questions.question: This exercise is ___ than I expected.

questions.def: 'More' forms the comparative of longer adjectives like 'serious'.
questions.question: The situation is ___ serious than we thought.

questions.def: Use 'the most + adjective' for superlatives with longer adjectives.
questions.question: He is ___ person I've ever met.

questions.def: Avoid double comparatives; use 'happier' or 'more happy'.
questions.question: She is more happier now than she was before.

questions.def: 'Worst' is the superlative form of 'bad'.
questions.question: This is the ___ movie I've seen this year.

questions.def: Use 'the more... the better...' for parallel increases in quality.
questions.question: The ___ expensive the restaurant, the better the food.

questions.def: 'As...as' compares equals; 'quite' adds nuance.
questions.question: He is ___ his brother.

questions.def: 'By far' emphasizes superlatives.
questions.question: This is by ___ the best solution.

questions.def: 'Not as...as' indicates a lower degree of something.
questions.question: She is ___ a good singer as her sister.

questions.def: Use 'longer' as the comparative of 'long' in this structure.
questions.question: The ___ you wait, the worse it will get.

questions.def: Use 'closer' as the comparative of 'close' in this structure.
questions.question: The ___ you look, the more you see.

questions.def: 'By far' is used to emphasize a superlative.
questions.question: This is ___ the most difficult question on the test.

questions.def: 'Foremost' means 'most important or best'.
questions.question: She is considered ___ expert in her field.

questions.def: 'Less' is used for uncountable nouns like 'experience'.
questions.question: She has ___ experience than I do.

questions.def: 'Even' emphasizes the comparative adjective.
questions.question: The project proved to be ___ more challenging than expected.

questions.def: 'By far' is an idiom to emphasize superlatives.
questions.question: This is by ___ the most efficient method.

questions.def: 'The better, the more' requires 'the' before 'more' for parallel increase.
questions.question: The better the weather, more people go to the beach.

questions.def: 'Later' is the comparative form of 'late'.
questions.question: It's ___ than I thought. I must leave now.

questions.def: 'Just as... as' emphasizes equality in comparison.
questions.question: He is ___ good at maths as his sister is.

questions.def: 'By far' is a common idiom to emphasize a superlative.
questions.question: She is by ___ the most qualified candidate.

questions.def: Double comparatives: 'the + comparative, the + comparative' shows parallel increase.
questions.question: The more I study, the ___ I feel.

questions.def: 'Less + adjective + than' compares two things showing one is smaller.
questions.question: This book is ___ that one.

questions.def: 'Best' is the superlative of 'good' for comparing three or more items.
questions.question: This is the ___ movie I've ever seen.

questions.def: 'As...as' is used for equal or negative comparisons.
questions.question: He is not as intelligent ___ his sister.

questions.def: 'Most' forms the superlative with long adjectives like 'expensive'.
questions.question: The ___ expensive car isn't always the best.
